items.q: What is the edit distance (the least number of single-letter changes) between 'kitten' and 'sitting'?
rationales: Two changes are not enough: k to s and e to i leave an extra g to add.
Three is the least: change k to s, change e to i, add g.

items.q: A program compares recognised text with the known text and the edit distance is 1 for a known text of 4 letters. What is the character error rate?
rationales: One would mean every letter was wrong; the rate is the distance divided by the length of the known text.
The rate divides by the length of the known text (4), not by 25.

items.q: For the line 'Order 4417-B shipped on 2026-10-13' Tesseract was told tessedit_char_whitelist=0123456789- . It returned '4417-02026-10-13'. What does that show?
options: The whitelist made Tesseract say it was unsure about the B
The B was forced into an allowed character, a 0, and the letters and spaces vanished
The whitelist only hides characters the engine already found
rationales: Tesseract gives no such warning; it picks the closest allowed character.
In this run the B became a 0, so a whitelist forces an answer instead of admitting doubt.

items.q: The timeout argument of image_to_string was set so short that Tesseract could not finish. Which exception did pytesseract 0.3.13 raise?
options: TimeoutError
RuntimeError
TesseractError
rationales: That is not what the wrapper raised in this study.
TesseractError is raised when Tesseract itself reports a failure, such as a missing language.

items.q: lang='ger' was passed to image_to_string for a German line. What happened, and what is the right code?
options: It worked, because ger is short for German
TesseractError: there is no ger.traineddata; the code is deu
It returned an empty string; the code is de
rationales: Tesseract uses ISO 639-3 codes such as deu, not 639-2 abbreviations.
Tesseract raised an error rather than returning an empty string; and de is not a Tesseract code.

items.q: A line holds the words 'The cat is' then 猫 then 'and the dog is' then 犬 then 'today'. What did lang='eng' alone give, and which setting read it right?
options: It gave 'The cat is 4 and the dog is % today'; lang='eng+jpn' read it right
It gave the whole line right; lang='jpn' broke it
It raised TesseractError; lang='jpn+eng' is the only order that works
rationales: English-only data has no Japanese characters, so it cannot give them right.
In this study both eng+jpn and jpn+eng read the line right and no error was raised.

items.q: A PDF has seven pages, spam0 to spam6. Which pages does the NAPS2 input 'spam.pdf[1:6:2]' take?
options: spam1, spam3 and spam5
spam2, spam4 and spam6
spam1 to spam6
rationales: The slice starts at index 1, not 2.
The step of 2 skips every other page.

items.q: subprocess.run(['python', '-c', 'raise SystemExit(2)'], check=True) is called. What happens?
options: It returns a result whose returncode is 2
It raises CalledProcessError with returncode 2
It raises FileNotFoundError
rationales: Without check=True it would return; check=True turns a failing exit status into an exception.
The program exists, so there is no FileNotFoundError.

items.q: A program opens output.txt three times with open('output.txt', 'a') and writes 'abc\n' each time. What does the file hold?
options: 'abc\n'

'abc
abc
abc
'
Nothing, because the file is opened again each time
rationales: Mode 'w' would leave one line; mode 'a' appends.
Append mode keeps what is there and adds to the end.

items.q: What does re.sub(r'-\n(\w)', r'\1', 'the half-\nextinguished light') return, and what does it show about joining hyphenated line ends in OCR text?
options: 'the half-extinguished light': the hyphen is kept
'the halfextinguished light': a real hyphen is removed too, so the joining can damage text
'the half extinguished light': a space replaces the hyphen
rationales: The pattern removes the hyphen and the line break.
The replacement has no space.

items.q: A line of text cropped tight to its letters was read as an empty string by Tesseract 5.3.4 in its default mode. Which change gave 'Tesseract reads this line' in this study?
options: Adding a white border of 10 pixels
Rotating the image by 12 degrees
Inverting it to white text on black
rationales: A tilt makes reading worse: five degrees already gave an error rate of 0.58.
Inverting is advice for white text on black, not the cause of an empty result here.
